clue.text: Dry obit amuses fans

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters of obit and amuses are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull obituary entertains admirers of the deceased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like a noun for admirers, but it is a verb telling you to spread out the ten letters of OBIT AMUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry in the sense of teetotal: someone abstemious refrains from alcohol and indulgence.

clue.text: Livid Tory

definitions.meaning: first meaning: livid is the bluish colour of a bruise
second meaning: ... is the Conservative party colour, so a Tory is a ...

explanation.walkthrough: Livid looks like furious, but its older sense is the bruise colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bruised colour and a supporter of Britain's Conservatives, whose colour it is.

clue.text: Booze upset half of folk

parts.note: to upset a vessel is to tip it over

indicators.note: half of keeps only one half of the folk word, its back half

parts.note: folk are people

explanation.surface: Drink has upset half the people present.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipple is a light word for alcoholic drink, as in 'what's your tipple?'

clue.text: Suited with tie and, primarily, evening dress

parts.note: a tie is a game or match

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letters of evening and dress

explanation.surface: Someone is dressed for the evening in a suit, tie and gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are suited go well together: they are matched or paired.

clue.text: Carry out robbery in prime locations?

indicators.note: keep only the letters at prime-numbered positions, the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: Should one obey orders to carry out a robbery in top neighbourhoods?
explanation.walkthrough: Prime locations sound like smart addresses; here they are positions 2, 3, 5 and 7 in ROBBERY, which keep O, B, E, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry out an order is to comply with it, to do as told.

clue.text: Son, ignoring fine, restrains dogs

indicators.note: ignoring means the fine letter is passed over and the son letter used in its place

parts.note: to fetter is to restrain with chains
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A son who didn't pay a fine has the dogs restraining him.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are a group of gundog breeds, such as the Irish setter.

clue.text: Former hospital north of state capital tackling oxygen fatigue

indicators.note: north of in a down clue puts the earlier pieces above the next

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: tackling means taking on and gripping, so the capital holds the oxygen letter

parts.note: Austin is the capital of the US state of Texas
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A former hospital in the capital treats patients with oxygen for fatigue.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaustion is extreme tiredness, a synonym for fatigue.

clue.text: Sociable guy at first argues about investing old capital

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of guy
investing means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the old capital
about signals the letters of argues turned around and rearranged

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until 1960

explanation.surface: A sociable man starts arguing about investing in old capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy looks like a name to use whole, but 'at first' wants only its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregarious describes someone fond of company, outgoing and friendly.

clue.text: Fence non-British fighter

indicators.note: non-British asks for the fighter's word with B, the abbreviation for British, taken away

parts.note: a boxer is a fighter in the ring

explanation.surface: A foreign boxer parries in a fencing bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like a verb about swordplay, but it is the noun: an oxer is a showjumping fence.
explanation.definitionFit: In showjumping an oxer is a spread obstacle built from two rails, a kind of jump.

clue.text: Sub-24-hour case completely obvious when one's arrested

parts.note: out can mean completely, as in an out-and-out rogue

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the obvious word holds the one inside it

parts.note: patent means plain, obvious
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A legal case looks obviously solid once someone has been arrested within a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' sounds legal, but it is a medical case: a patient treated without an overnight stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital patient who is treated and leaves the same day, never admitted for a night.

clue.text: Perhaps Edinburgh University Press called by Thursday

indicators.note: by means beside, so the call word sits next to the day

parts.note: called on the phone, rang

explanation.surface: A Scottish academic publisher got a phone call on Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: The press is not a publisher but a crowd: THRANG is the Scots form of throng, a press of people, which might be found at a university in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrang is a Scots word for a throng or crush of people, so a crowd at an Edinburgh college is an example.

clue.text: Bury hosting guide on vacation number two?

indicators.note: hosting means containing a guest, so the burial word holds the next piece

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so guide loses its middle letters and keeps only its ends

explanation.surface: The town of Bury has a tour guide away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb. The question mark signals that two is only one example of the whole numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is a whole number, one example of an integer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One famous key suspect in compiler's book?

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or dodgy, so the letters of famous key are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-known clue proves to be dubious in a crossword setter's collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The compiler is the setter speaking of themself, so 'in compiler's book' is 'in my opinion'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase gives a personal opinion, as 'in my book' does, with the compiler being the speaker.

clue.text: Advance, say, bombed nation rued

indicators.note: bombed means wrecked and blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation regretted its advance after being bombed.
explanation.walkthrough: Advance looks like a military push, but it is the name of a British trade union in financial services; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance is a British workers' organisation, so it is an example of a labour union.

clue.text: Rake new riverside port

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roué

explanation.surface: A new libertine arrives in a port on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is a French city on the Seine with a large inland river port.

clue.text: Nick's Kindle found in Turkey

indicators.note: found in says the kindle word sits inside the country's code

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
to kindle feelings is to rouse them

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick has his e-reader discovered in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle looks like the e-reader brand but is the verb. To trouser is British slang for pocketing something, often dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for pocketing or stealing something, often money.

clue.text: Fine wearing crown in wine region

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the crown has the fine word inside it

parts.note: a taj is a crown or tall headdress
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: Something fine is worn as a crown in a wine-producing area.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokaj is a Hungarian area famous for its sweet dessert wines.

clue.text: Bash one side of elbow in fighting arenas

parts.note: a bash is a party, as is a do

indicators.note: one side of asks for just half of the elbow word, its first three letters

parts.note: to elbow someone is to jostle them

explanation.surface: Someone strikes one side of their elbow during a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dojos are the halls where martial arts such as judo and karate are trained and practised.

clue.text: Jazz fan banned from Mexican state capital

indicators.note: banned from means shut out, so the jazz fan is taken out of the state

parts.note: Yucatan is a state of Mexico
a cat is jazz slang for a fan or player

explanation.surface: A jazz enthusiast is barred from entering the capital of a Mexican state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' seems to belong with Mexican state, but it stands alone as money.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means money, and the yuan is the currency of China.

clue.text: Queen of Carthage arguably lazed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the legendary founder and queen of Carthage in the Aeneid
second meaning: lazing is arguably doing nothing, with O as nought

explanation.surface: One might argue the Carthaginian queen spent her days lounging about.
explanation.walkthrough: Lazing about is doing nothing; split the answer as DID O, with O as nought, and 'arguably' plus the question mark admit the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid, Dido founds and rules Carthage and loves Aeneas.

clue.text: What, in court, recalled convalescence?

indicators.note: in places the what word inside the reversed court word
recalled is read as called back, so the court word runs backwards

parts.note: the bar is the court, the legal profession
eh? is what you say when you have not heard: what?

explanation.surface: A witness asks 'What?' in court as a statement is recalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is the period of rehabilitation and recovery after illness or addiction.

clue.text: One might amend section of flight around outskirts of Venice when heading north

indicators.note: around says the stair word goes round the Venice letters

parts.note: a riser is the upright part of one stair in a flight

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means going upward, so the letters run backwards
the outskirts are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of Venice

explanation.surface: A flight approaching Venice heads north round the outskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight looks like air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviser is someone who corrects and amends a text.

clue.text: Labour uprising crushing most unpleasant polled assembly of Young Cons?

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing round, so the reversed party holds the other letters
uprising in a down clue means reading upward, backwards

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour party

indicators.note: polled means with the head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: worst means most unpleasant

explanation.surface: A Labour revolt crushes the nastiest gathering of Young Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Young Cons look like Young Conservatives, but they are young convicts: a borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Borstals were British institutions holding young offenders, a gathering of juvenile convicts.

clue.text: Tidy after uniform's put away? Not yet

indicators.note: after places the tidy word behind the uniform letter

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to neaten is to tidy

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tidy up once their uniform is put away, but has not done it yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' looks like stowing the uniform, but it means eaten, as food is put away.
explanation.definitionFit: Food not yet consumed has not been put away, the idiom for eaten.

clue.text: Hacks New Orleans in, say, Mardi Gras' finale

indicators.note: in places the city's letters within the others

parts.note: Mardi is Tuesday in French, a day, say: French jour

indicators.note: finale is the end, so the last letter of Gras

explanation.surface: Journalists descend on New Orleans for the end of Mardi Gras.
explanation.walkthrough: Mardi Gras pretends to be the carnival; here Mardi is just one French day, jour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacks and journos are both informal, slightly scornful words for journalists.

clue.text: Knocking sound due to rising oil temperature

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upward, so the oil word runs backwards

parts.note: attar is a fragrant oil from rose petals

explanation.surface: An engine knocks because the oil temperature is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: Oil suggests engine oil, but it is attar, the perfume oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-tat imitates the noise of rapping on a door.

clue.text: Appreciation shown by international instructor in 16

parts.note: an appreciation of something is a sense of it

explanation.surface: A martial-arts teacher from abroad shows appreciation to students.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensei is the Japanese title for a teacher of martial arts in a dojo.

clue.text: Ascending bird almost finding polar feature

indicators.note: ascending in a down clue means reading upward, backwards
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A bird flying upward nearly reaches something in the polar ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg, short for iceberg, is a floating mass of ice in polar seas.

clue.text: Picked up Cockney who is getting over drink

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so this is a sound-alike

parts.note: a Cockney drops the h, so who's becomes 'oo's, and over is O in cricket: together said 'oo's O

explanation.surface: A Londoner is overheard getting over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oo's O, said aloud, gives the Greek spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouzo is a Greek aniseed-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: Stomach problem?

parts.note: stomach is the verb, to put up with, so this is enduring a difficulty to the end

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as indigestion, but stomach means tolerate: to put up with a problem until it passes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to endure an unpleasant situation patiently until it is over.

clue.text: Show behind time, one leaving agitation

indicators.note: leaving means the time and one letters depart from the agitation word

parts.note: agitation is motion, stirring
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A show running behind time leaves one performer agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show behind' reads as running late; it means baring your buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is to display your bare backside as a prank.

clue.text: Helping to secure backed-up sled order

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the helping word holds the sled inside it

parts.note: a helping is a portion or ration

indicators.note: backed-up says the sled word runs backwards

parts.note: a luge is a racing sled

explanation.surface: A queue of sledders is backed up waiting for their orders to be served.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulation is a rule or official order.
